question.text: Long-term capital gains on equity mutual funds (held > 12 months) exceeding Rs. 1.25 lakh per year are taxed at:

explanation.text: The Logic: Long-term capital gains on equity-oriented mutual funds (units held for more than 12 months) are taxed under Section 112A. The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 raised the Section 112A LTCG rate from 10% to 12.5% and raised the annual exemption threshold from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 1.25 lakh for transfers on or after 23 July 2024. So gains above the Rs. 1.25 lakh annual exemption are taxed at 12.5% (plus applicable surcharge and cess). The Trap: 10% was the pre-July-2024 Section 112A rate. 15% is the (legacy) equity STCG rate, not the LTCG rate. 20% is the current equity STCG / certain other rates, not the equity LTCG rate. Note: The specific 12.5% / Rs. 1.25 lakh threshold for equity-MF LTCG is not stated on the cited pages of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook, which on the pages checked discusses FoF taxation and debt fund / FMP features rather than the direct equity-MF LTCG rule. The framing above is general FY 2025-26 Indian income-tax knowledge.
